message.content:

1. Q
2. (R ↔ P)
3. Q

- Q (stated in premises 1 and 3)
- R ↔ P (stated in premise 2)

- R ↔ P (reiteration)

Given that Q appears twice and R ↔ P appears once, the most logical conclusion that combines all information would be:

Q ∧ (R ↔ P)
